provenance_findings.note: TDL identifies G. S. Ananthanarayanan as author of a Tamil shorthand manual published by the Tamil Nadu government in 1965. This corroborates professional shorthand expertise but does not alone prove authorship of the Acharya volumes.

The retrospective recollection says the Tamil shorthand book was printed by the government in 1964, while TDL's institutional catalog records publication year 1965. Do not silently reconcile the discrepancy; inspect edition/front matter.

Part 1's 1958 preface directly states that 'Sri Ananthan' took the Mylapore discourses in shorthand, typed copies were made, and the material was arranged for publication. The relation is therefore established at collection level. The printed prose remains editorially mediated and is not assumed verbatim.
Part 2's 1974 publisher preface states that Parts 1 and 3 had already been published. Part 3's existence is therefore publisher-confirmed, but its scan and exact edition metadata remain unresolved.
Part 2's 1974 publisher preface says Part 4 would appear shortly. This is an announcement, not proof that Part 4 was actually published.
The 1974 publisher preface says the books were issued with Mahaperiyava's blessing. Pramana does not infer personal proofreading, correction, or approval of every printed wording from that statement.
